requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST tell agents that the requirements commit may fail validation until evidence is authored, and that only the pull request as a whole must pass.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The `habeas-requirements` skill must tell agents two things: the requirements commit may fail validation until evidence is authored, and only the pull request as a whole must pass.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_expects_the_requirements_commit_to_fail_validation]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It calls `assert_phrases("habeas-requirements", ...)`. That helper builds the bundled skill text (`SKILL.md` plus its reference files, whitespace-collapsed) with `bundled_skill`. It then asserts with `assert_text` that the text contains the phrase "This commit fails validation until evidence is authored; that is expected, as only the pull request as a whole must pass".

That one sentence carries both parts of the obligation:
- The commit fails validation until evidence is authored, and that is expected.
- Only the pull request as a whole must pass.

The assertion would fail if the skill dropped or reworded the sentence. The test also targets the right skill, `habeas-requirements`. The text names no other scenarios, modes or boundaries.

I did not read the skill file itself. Under the testing criteria, a test that checks the skill text for the required statement is the appropriate kind of test here, so I found no gap.
